decisions.quote:
In this study we tried to replicate the unconscious
thought advantage (UTA), which states that complex decisions are
better handled by unconscious thinking. We designed an experiment
in e-prime using similar material as the original study (choosing
between four different apartments, each described by 12 attributes).
A total of 73 participants (52 women (71.2%); 18 to 62 age:
M=24.63; SD=8.7) took part in the experiment.
decisions.reason: Both the shipped record and the blind coder agree that the paper is a completed replication collecting new experimental data (N = 73) in the four-apartment decision task to re-test the unconscious thought advantage.

corrected_value.title: Think different: the merits of unconscious thought in preference development and decision making.

decisions.quote:
The main outcome variable was, similar as in
Dijksterhuis´s [2] study, the difference in evaluation of the
most desirable and the most undesirable apartment. We
followed Dijksterhuis´s rationale that recognizing and
rejecting a particular unattractive alternative is in many cases
as important as choosing the right one.
decisions.location: Section I.C, Aims and Rationale of Our Study of UTT (lines 197-202); see also Section II.B (lines 256-259), Section IV (lines 455-457), and References [2] (lines 662-664)
decisions.reason: The shipped record points to Reference [1] (Dijksterhuis & Nordgren, 2006, 'A Theory of Unconscious Thought'), which is a theoretical review paper cited for the general tenets of Unconscious Thought Theory, whereas Reference [3] (Strick et al., 2011) is a meta-analysis. Under the codebook rule to rule out review/theory and meta-analytic works in favor of the primary empirical study whose finding is re-tested, the primary empirical target is Reference [2] (Dijksterhuis, 2004, doi:10.1037/0022-3514.87.5.586), whose four-apartment, 12-attribute decision paradigm across immediate, conscious, and unconscious thought conditions and primary outcome measure (difference in evaluation between the most desirable and most undesirable apartment) this experiment directly replicates.

decisions.quote:
In conclusion, we did not replicate the results suggested by
UTT. However, from the present study we cannot conclude
whether this was the case of flaws in the theory or flaws in our
experiment.
decisions.location: Section IV, Discussion (lines 551-554); see also Abstract (lines 17-20) and Section IV (line 458)
decisions.reason: Both the shipped record and the blind coder agree on 'failed'. The authors explicitly state their overall verdict that they did not succeed in replicating the unconscious thought advantage (no significant differences across conditions in apartment evaluation or best-apartment rating, F = 2.110, p = .129 and F = 2.159, p = .123).
